title: Scenario schema v0.2 (also reads v0.1)
description: What happens to a circuit's inputs over time. A scenario names a circuit file, lists the input ports it drives, and gives a list of steps, each with the value of some inputs and a duration in integer time units. An input not mentioned in a step keeps its previous value; the first step must set every input. Levels are the strings "0", "1", "X" (unknown) and "Z" (floating). Version 0.2 adds two optional fields: `initial` (the stored state of flip-flops and latches before step 0) and `force` (a net held at a level over a range of steps); a 0.1 file may not use them. Structure only: that the circuit exists and has these input ports is a separate semantic check (see validate/).

schema.description: Format and version. Readers reject an unknown major version.

id.description: Name of this scenario, e.g. full_adder_all_inputs.

circuit.description: Path of the circuit file, relative to the repository root and using forward slashes, e.g. "examples/full_adder.json".

circuit_id.description: Optional: the id the circuit file is expected to have, so a mismatch is detected.

inputs.description: Ids of the circuit's input ports this scenario drives, in display order.

steps.description: Consecutive intervals of time. Step 0 starts at time 0.

initial.description: Since 0.2. Element id to the level its stored state has before step 0 (Q of a flip-flop or latch). Without it the state is X. Only elements with state may be named. A clock edge, preset or clear changes it as normal; the start of step 0 is not a clock edge.

force.description: Since 0.2. Nets held at a level whatever drives them, over a range of steps. Everything that reads the net sees the forced level; when the range ends the net returns to its driven value. Force beats element outputs and scenario inputs on that net.

net.description: Id of a net in the circuit.

to.description: Last step held (inclusive). Absent: to the end.

duration.description: Length of the step in integer time units.

values.description: Input id to level, for the inputs that change at the start of this step.
